en.name: Chives
en.summary: Chives keep 1–2 weeks at room temperature and 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below. They are a hollow, high-moisture leaf, so the whole game is keeping them from either drying out or sitting wet.
en.pantry: 1–2 weeks with the cut ends standing in a little water, out of direct sun, like a small bunch of flowers. Change the water daily and re-trim the ends when you do. Chives are hollow tubes full of water, and on a dry worktop they wilt and go papery within days, while a bunch left sealed in a plastic bag at room temperature turns to slime even faster. A glass of water and open air is the compromise that actually works.
en.fridge: 2–3 weeks at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, which is where chives do best. Wrap the bunch loosely in dry kitchen paper and put it in a bag or box in the crisper — the paper takes up the moisture the chives give off, which is what otherwise pools and rots them from the cut ends. Do not wash them until you use them, and check the bunch every few days, pulling out any stem that has gone soft before it takes its neighbours with it.
en.freezer: Freeze damage will appear, so no freezer timeline is given. Chives are mostly water, and freezing bursts the cells: what comes out is dark, limp and wet, with no structure at all. That said, chopped chives frozen flat in a bag are perfectly usable stirred into a potato soup, an omelette or a butter at the last moment — you simply cannot garnish with them. Snipping them fresh is always better if you have them.
en.thawing: Do not thaw chopped chives before use; add them to the dish straight from frozen so they do not collapse into a wet clump.
spoilage: Slimy, darkened stems, usually starting at the cut ends.
A sour or sulphurous smell rather than a clean, oniony one.
Yellowing stems that have dried to paper.
Water in the bag or box that has gone cloudy and smells.
tips: Wrap in dry kitchen paper; it is the moisture they give off that rots them.
Snip with scissors rather than chopping with a knife — a knife bruises them.
Add them at the very end of cooking; heat destroys the flavour quickly.
Freeze a flat bag of snipped chives for cooking, not for garnish.

faq.a: 1–2 weeks at room temperature with the stems in water, or 2–3 weeks in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
Freeze damage will appear, so no timeline is given. Frozen chives are limp and wet but still fine stirred into a cooked dish; they cannot be used as a garnish.

faq.q: How do you stop chives going slimy in the fridge?
faq.a: Wrap them loosely in dry kitchen paper inside a bag or box, do not wash them until use, and pull out any soft stems as soon as you spot them.

zh.name: 細香蔥
zh.summary: 細香蔥放常溫可放 1～2 週，放 4 °C 以下冷藏則是 2～3 週。它是中空、含水量高的葉子，所以整件事的重點就是：既不能讓它乾掉，也不能讓它一直濕著。
zh.pantry: 把切口插進一點水裡、避免直曬，像一小束花那樣，1～2 週。每天換水，換的時候順手把末端重新剪一下。細香蔥是裝滿水的中空管子，放在乾燥的檯面上幾天就會萎軟、變得像紙；而密封在塑膠袋裡放常溫的那一把，爛得更快。一杯水加上通風，才是真正行得通的折衷。
zh.fridge: 放 4 °C 以下 2～3 週，這也是細香蔥表現最好的地方。請用乾的廚房紙巾把整束鬆鬆地包起來，再裝進袋子或盒子放蔬果室——紙巾會吸掉細香蔥自己散出的水氣，而那些水氣如果積起來，就會從切口把它爛掉。要用時才洗；每隔幾天檢查一次，看到變軟的那幾根就先挑掉，免得拖累旁邊的。
zh.freezer: 冷凍會出現凍傷，所以沒有給期限。細香蔥幾乎都是水，冷凍會把細胞撐破：拿出來的東西顏色深、軟塌、濕濕的，完全沒有結構。不過話說回來，切好後平鋪冷凍的細香蔥，在起鍋前拌進馬鈴薯濃湯、蛋捲或奶油裡完全好用——你只是不能拿它擺盤。手邊有新鮮的話，當然還是現剪最好。
zh.thawing: 切好的冷凍細香蔥不要先解凍，直接從冷凍加進菜裡，才不會塌成一團濕泥。
spoilage: 蔥管變黏滑、顏色變深，通常從切口開始。
聞起來酸或有硫味，而不是乾淨的蔥香。
袋子或盒子裡積的水變混濁並且有味道。
tips: 用乾廚房紙巾包起來；爛掉的元凶是它自己散出的水氣。
用剪刀剪而不是用刀切，刀會壓傷它。
起鍋前才放；加熱很快就會把香氣毀掉。
切好平鋪冷凍一袋當料理用，不要當擺盤用。

faq.a: 莖插水放常溫 1～2 週，或 4 °C 以下冷藏 2～3 週。
冷凍會凍傷，所以沒有給期限。凍過的細香蔥軟濕，拌進煮好的菜裡還是好用，但不能當擺盤。

faq.q: 細香蔥放冰箱怎麼避免變黏滑？
faq.a: 用乾廚房紙巾鬆鬆包好、裝進袋子或盒子，要用時才洗，看到軟掉的就立刻挑掉。
